analysis: Reviewed SSDPrefixCache.swift head units (donate/stage/readWindowSidecars and the eviction section). The only changed lines are 1773-1778: evictOldestEntry now delegates victim selection to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:) with a closure that calls retireIndexedEntries([url]). The previous inline loop iterated index.oldestEntries(), skipped undeletable entries, and returned 0 on externalChange. Its replacement lives in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement, which is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that it keeps three behaviors: (1) it skips a valid-but-undeletable victim rather than stalling the LRU budget; (2) it aborts on externalChange; (3) it is bounded. That is an unverified contract, not a demonstrated regression. The visible parts of the change keep their guards: hasSafeRoot is still checked first, and retireIndexedEntries still goes through removalLock, hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot, then SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with the root and epochStore. Eviction stats are still recorded when bytes are freed. The donation and staging paths (lines 657-1593) are unchanged, and I saw no regression there. HMAC lookup tags, the salt-scoped tags, the donation gate, the weightHash/layoutEpoch/lookupTag binding checks, corrupt-file deletion and KEK-bound decryption all remain. T-041 at-rest posture (HMAC names, 30-minute TTL, LRU disk budget, KEK purge) is not weakened by the visible lines. Integration should check that the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest implementation preserves the skip-undeletable, externalChange-abort and bounded-iteration semantics, because a stuck LRU eviction would let the cache exceed its disk budget (an availability and at-rest retention concern under T-041).
